requirements.requirement: Configure the opsadmin account on node1 with the specified SSH public key.
requirements.summary: The account exists with the expected home and shell, and its securely owned authorized_keys file contains the exact requested ED25519 key. The account, key, and permissions remained present after restart.

Effective sshd policy requires public-key authentication and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication. Password-only connections were rejected before and after restart, while sshd remained active and listening.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and coherent: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and recovered sshd, account, key, permissions, and authentication policy. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No successful end-to-end SSH login using the specified key was captured, presumably because only the public key was supplied. Confidence rests on the exact authorized_keys content, secure permissions, valid effective sshd policy, active listener, and negative password-authentication tests.
The captured output omits the result of passwd -S and redacts portions of the password-generation command, so the precise password-state details cannot be independently reviewed.

operational_hygiene.summary: System health remained clean: sshd recovered, no failed services appeared, package health remained good, and socket and temporary-file changes were normal restart effects. One unnecessary retained mutation occurred: cmd-9534c4d7a2b14b84 generated and assigned opsadmin a password even though SSH was configured as key-only. This did not contribute to the required outcome and left a password credential on the account, although SSH policy prevents its use for authentication. The transient reboot units disappeared after restart and left no observed residue.
